title: Lumen Expands Quantum Footprint with Ohio State Fiber Research and Fortinet PQC SASE Rollout - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Lumen Technologies is funding Ohio State University research on sending non-classical light and doing quantum sensing over deployed commercial fiber. Separately, it is adding Fortinet's NIST-standardized post-quantum cryptography to its managed SASE service, with a customer preview in November 2026 and general availability in January 2027.

insights.claim: The no-cloning theorem rules out standard erbium-doped fiber amplifiers for quantum signals. That leaves fiber loss and polarization drift as hard limits on linking geographically separated quantum computing clusters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum networking needs repeaters and other new infrastructure, not just existing telecom amplification.
insights.quote: the quantum no-cloning theorem prohibits the use of standard erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) to boost optical signals
insights.locator: Connecting geographically separated quantum computing clusters

insights.claim: Lumen is funding Ohio State research into how field-deployed commercial fiber carries single-photon and entangled states, to set empirical channel bounds for optical repeaters and dispersion management.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A Tier-1 carrier is positioning its fiber footprint as future quantum-network infrastructure.
insights.locator: Connecting geographically separated quantum computing clusters

insights.claim: The project also tests distributed quantum sensing, using optical noise backscatter along fiber corridors to detect seismic anomalies, cable strain and other environmental changes that degrade fiber health.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum sensing could pay off sooner than quantum transport, as a network monitoring tool.

insights.claim: To address harvest-now, decrypt-later risk, Lumen is building Fortinet's PQC libraries (FIPS 203 ML-KEM and FIPS 204 ML-DSA) into its managed SASE edge. The goal is a crypto-agile move away from RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography without replacing underlying hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQC is becoming a managed-service product that carriers and security vendors can sell to enterprises now.
insights.quote: The integrated service aims to give enterprise customers a crypto-agile path to transition corporate wide-area networks away from vulnerable RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography

insights.claim: The Fortinet PQC-enabled SASE service will roll out in phases: customer preview starting November 2026 and general availability planned for January 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This gives a concrete commercial timeline for enterprise PQC adoption through managed networks.

insights.claim: Lumen also announced an exploratory pilot with Emerald AI to steer AI compute workloads across its network dynamically, based on power grid availability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Power constraints are pushing network operators toward energy-aware routing of AI workloads.
